overview: This file traces U.S. intelligence about Japan’s rubber supply and manufacturing capabilities from 1938 to 1943. It begins with a report that Japan unsuccessfully offered $1 million for DuPont’s synthetic-rubber process, then includes two copies of a Chungking despatch describing Japanese military rubber ski boots, insulated or shock-absorbing boots, and protective garments. The largest group of documents records information supplied by a former Dunlop factory manager about tire-production capacity, shortages and substitutes for naphtha and carbon black, the extensive use and stockpiling of reclaimed rubber, chemical and rayon plants near Kyoto, Japanese tire-making machinery, and the possible substitution of treated rayon for cotton tire cord.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japan’s attempt to purchase DuPont’s synthetic-rubber process
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s unsuccessful effort to purchase DuPont’s synthetic-rubber manufacturing process in order to reduce dependence on imported natural rubber.
subfiles.summary: DuPont rejects Japan's $1 million offer for its synthetic-rubber process; Japan also failed to get Germany's.

subfiles.title: Chungking despatch on new Japanese military uses for rubber
subfiles.about: Relays Chinese intelligence concerning Japanese rubber footwear and gas-protective garments intended principally for military use.
subfiles.summary: Wang reports Japanese troops testing rubber ski boots and gas-protective gear, showing rubber use remains mostly military, for sharing with economic-warfare agencies.

subfiles.title: Duplicate copy of Chungking despatch on Japanese rubber equipment
subfiles.about: A second copy of the despatch reporting Japanese military and civilian uses of rubber.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate despatch repeats Wang's intelligence on Japanese rubber ski boots, gas gear, and limited civilian uses, for wider distribution.

subfiles.title: Allison letter forwarding intelligence from former Dunlop manager Morton
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum and factory sketch based on a conference with a former Dunlop Tire Company manager in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Allison forwards a former Dunlop manager's intelligence on Japanese tire and carbon-black production, with a factory sketch.

subfiles.title: Economic Warfare Division memorandum on the Japanese rubber industry
subfiles.from: Fowler Hamilton and John M. Allison
subfiles.to: Gregory Hewlett, as an enclosure to the covering letter
subfiles.about: Records Mr. Morton’s detailed assessment of Japan’s rubber supply, tire factories, substitute materials, chemical plants, and machinery-production capacity.
subfiles.summary: Morton details Japan's worsening rubber-material shortages, reclaimed-rubber tire production, and comparable tire-making machinery, naming cotton supply as the main output constraint.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A: sketch of factories in the Kyoto district
subfiles.from: Mr. Morton, as source for Fowler Hamilton and John M. Allison
subfiles.to: Gregory Hewlett, with the accompanying memorandum
subfiles.about: Provides the rough geographic sketch used to locate a chemical plant and a suspected rayon plant near Mount Hiei.
subfiles.summary: Exhibit sketch depicts a chemical plant and a probable rayon plant in Kyoto's district.

interest: Shows Japan's wartime push for rubber self-sufficiency, from a failed DuPont bid to military rubber-gear innovations.
